RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the October 24, 2008/Kartika 2, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
35
Import of pulses
*101. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has recently
decided to import pulses from foreign
countries to augment domestic availability
and to check its rising prices;
(b) if so, the details thereof and under
what terms and conditions such imports of
pulses have been allowed;
(c) whether the indigenous production
of pulses has fallen in the past few years;
(d) if so, the factors responsible for fall
in production of pulses; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
encourage production of pulses in the
country and to avoid its import?
Import of pulses by Public Sector
institutions
†*102 SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that pulses have
been imported by public sector institutions
to meet the demand of pulses by consumers
and control their prices in the country;
(b) if so, the names of the institutions
which have imported pulses and the
quantity of pulses imported by them in
the years 2005, 2006, 2007 and till
September, 2008;
(c) the average cost of each pulse after
its import in India during the said period;
and
(d) the cost at which imported pulses
were sold by these institutions in the
country?
Railway projects in the North Eastern
Region
*103. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the length of railways in the whole
of the country and that in the North-Eastern
States;

36
(b) the length of the broad-gauge and
metre-gauge railway lines in the different
States of the country;
(c) the details of status of gauge
conversion in the North-Eastern States; and
(d) the status of construction of new
lines in the North-Eastern States?
Rottening of grains in FCI godowns
†*104. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister  of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the quantity of grains rotted in the
godowns of Food Corporation of India
during the period 2005 to September, 2008;
(b) the market price of the rotted grains
together with the amount that had to be
spent to lift the same;
(c) the reasons for the rottening of
grains alongwith the names of the officers
found responsible for it; and
(d) the steps taken to ensure non-
rottening of grains in the godowns of Food
Corporation of India in future?
Health scenario in the country
*105. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister  of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of programmes being
implemented under the National Rural
Health Mission in the country;
(b) the targets fixed for 2007-08 and the
achievements thereof, alongwith the details
in respect of Rajasthan;
(c) the status of health scenario in the
country, programme-wise and where
Rajasthan stands in this regard; and
(d) in what manner various national
parameters of rural health in the country
compare with the developing and
developed countries?
Absorption of porters/coolies as fourth
grade employees
*106. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister  of RAILW AYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has decided that porters/coolies would be
absorbed as fourth grade employees;
(b) if so, whether they would be given
the scale of fourth grade employees; and
(c) if so, whether passengers would not
be required to pay porters/coolies?
Deficit in rainfall in certain areas
*107. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister  of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Peninsular
India was facing deficit in rainfall from
South-West Monsoon during the period
15 June—15 July;
(b) if so, whether there are areas where
deficit has been more than 40 per cent and
whether in those areas there has been no
sowing or the seeds sown have not
germinated;
(c) whether the situation was aggravated
by the very poor prospects of monsoon rains
reviving in these areas before August; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

37
(d) if so, whether Government has sent
teams to the affected States to assess the
‘scarcity’ conditions prevalent and to make
an estimate of relief funds that would be
needed to tackle the emergency?
